# Model and source

* Citation: Guiastrennec B, Sonne DP, Bergstrand M, Vilsboll T, Knop FK,
  Karlsson MO (2018). Model-Based Prediction of Plasma Concentration and
  Enterohepatic Circulation of Total Bile Acids in Humans. CPT
  Pharmacometrics Syst Pharmacol 7(9):603-612.
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1002/psp4.12325>
* PubMed Central: <https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC6157686/>
* Upstream gastric-emptying model: Guiastrennec B et al. (2016) CPT
  Pharmacometrics Syst Pharmacol 5(12):692-700,
  <https://doi.org/10.1002/psp4.12152>.

The model describes what happens to the body's pool of total bile acids
(TBA) after a test drink. The drink is dosed in kcal into the stomach.
Gastric emptying is inhibited by the calories already in the upper small
intestine and switches on with a logistic onset after the drink. The
calories that reach the duodenum, converted into a fat-equivalent amount
(Eq. 1), increase the rate at which the gallbladder empties (Eq. 3). That
emptying is interrupted by a postprandial refilling window (Eq. 2), which
is what produces the second TBA peak. Bile from the gallbladder carries
113 mM TBA into the upper small intestine. There a fraction FAU is
absorbed and the rest transits a three-compartment lower small
intestine, from which it is absorbed. Both routes lead to the liver,
which returns a constant fraction EH to the gallbladder. The rest spills
over into a two-compartment plasma distribution taken from radiolabelled
cholic-acid data. The TBA pool is closed: the model has no faecal loss
and no hepatic synthesis, because the authors assumed the two cancel.

The model was built from the authors' NONMEM code (Supplementary
Figure S2), with final estimates from Table 2 and Supplementary Table S3.

```{r load-model}
mod <- readModelDb("Guiastrennec_2018_bile_acids")
ui <- rxode2::rxode2(mod)
```

# Population

Thirty adults (15 with type 2 diabetes and 15 healthy controls matched on
sex, age and body-mass index) each drank four test drinks in a crossover
after a 10-hour fast (Supplementary Table S1): 18 men and 12 women, mean
age 60 years (42-71), mean weight 86.2 kg (63.6-122), mean height 1.76 m.
The study gave 920 gallbladder volumes (ultrasound, -10 to 60 min) and
1,236 plasma TBA concentrations (molar sum of 12 bile acids, -20 to
240 min).

```{r population}
str(ui$population)
```

The four test drinks (Table 1) are the dosing inputs of the model:

```{r drinks}
drinks <- tibble::tibble(
  drink = factor(
    c("OGTT 75 g", "Low fat", "Medium fat", "High fat"),
    levels = c("OGTT 75 g", "Low fat", "Medium fat", "High fat")
  ),
  DOSE_FAT_G = c(0, 2.5, 10, 40),
  DOSE_CARB_G = c(75, 107, 93, 32),
  DOSE_PROT_G = c(0, 13, 11, 3),
  DRINK_OGTT = c(1, 0, 0, 0),
  FED_HIGHFAT = c(0, 0, 0, 1)
) |>
  mutate(kcal = 4 * DOSE_CARB_G + 4 * DOSE_PROT_G + 9 * DOSE_FAT_G)
knitr::kable(drinks)
# Table 1 prints the energy as 300 / 503 / 506 / 500 kcal.
stopifnot(all(abs(drinks$kcal - c(300, 503, 506, 500)) <= 0.5))
```

# Source trace

| Model element | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Fat-equivalent amount in duodenum | `efat = x3 / kcal * (fat + Pprot*prot + Pcarb*carb)` | Eq. 1; Figure S2 code `X3S` |
| Gallbladder refilling window | logistic onset at `Trefill_onset`, offset at `Trefill_onset + Trefill_duration` | Eq. 2; Figure S2 code `RELAX` |
| Gallbladder emptying rate | `GBvol * KRB * (1 + Slopeefat * efat) * GBrefill` | Eq. 3; Figure S2 code `DADT(4)` |
| HLRB, T2D effect | `1250 * (1 - 0.481 * DIS_DIAB)` min | Eq. 4; Table 2 |
| Slopeefat, age and T2D effects | `101 * (1 - 0.025 * (AGE - 64)) * (1 - 0.329 * DIS_DIAB)` | Eq. 5; Table 2 |
| MTTA,L, sex and carbohydrate effects | `109 * (1 - 0.279 * SEXF) * (1 + 0.00614 * (DOSE_CARB_G - 93))` min | Eq. 6; Table 2 |
| `lbase_gb` | log(29.4) mL for 70 kg | Table 2 |
| `lhldj` | log(2.52) min | Table 2 |
| `pcarb`, `pprot`, `pfat` | 0.0574, 0.823, 1 (fixed) | Table 2 |
| `slope_refill`, `ltrefill_onset`, `ltrefill_dur` | 0.155, log(25.6), log(156) | Table 2 |
| `lhltul` | log(59.7) min | Table 2 |
| `logitfau`, `e_drink_ogtt_fau` | logit(0.216), +1.25 on the logit | Table 2; Figure S2 code `THETA(16)` |
| `logiteh`, `e_fed_highfat_eh` | logit(0.638), -0.294 on the logit | Table 2; Figure S2 code `THETA(18)` |
| `gb_cc` | 113 mM, fixed | Table 2 |
| `lqh`, `e_fed_qh` | log(1.5) L/min, +30% after the drink, fixed | Table 2; Figure S2 code `TVQH` |
| `lvc`, `lvp`, `lq` | log(2.839) L, log(4.072) L, log(0.1732) L/min, fixed | Table 2; Figure S3; Figure S2 code |
| Liver volume | `0.822 * BSA^(1.108 * AGE^-0.022)`, DuBois BSA | Methods (Small et al.); Figure S2 code `VH` |
| Allometric scaling | volumes `(WT/70)^1`, flows `(WT/70)^0.75` | Methods; Table 2 footnote b |
| Initial conditions | fasting steady state | Figure S2 code `A_0` block |
| `ramax`, `km` | 2.292 kcal/min, 25.12 kcal, fixed | Table 2; Figure S2 code |
| `lkg0`, `lkul`, `lslpcal`, `e_sexf_slpcal` | log(1.06), log(0.0266), log(0.0173), 0.407, fixed | Guiastrennec 2016 Table 3 |
| `steep`, `lt50ogtt`, `lt50fat` | 0.285, log(15.7), log(23.1), fixed | Guiastrennec 2016 Table 3 and Eq. 3 |
| Eta block (8 x 8) | variances and covariances | Supplementary Table S3 |
| `etalkg0`, `etalkul`, `etalslpcal` | 1.55^2, 0.56^2, 0.19^2, fixed | Guiastrennec 2016 Table 3 |
| `propSd` | 0.318 | Table 2 (TBA) |
| `propSd_GVol`, `addSd_GVol` | 0.102, sqrt(4.27) = 2.066 mL | Table 2 (gallbladder); Figure S2 `$SIGMA` |

# Simulation helpers

The drink is dosed into `stomach` at time 0. The model declares two
endpoints, plasma TBA (`Cc`) and gallbladder volume (`GVol`). Each
observation row therefore names an endpoint with `dvid`. Both outputs
come back as columns on every row whichever endpoint is named.

```{r helpers}
obs_times <- c(0, 5, 10, 15, 20, 30, 40, 45, 60, 75, 90, 105, 120, 150, 180, 210, 240)

make_events <- function(n_per_drink, subject = list(WT = 70, HT = 170, AGE = 64, SEXF = 0, DIS_DIAB = 0)) {
  bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(drinks)), function(i) {
    ids <- (i - 1L) * n_per_drink + seq_len(n_per_drink)
    dose <- tibble::tibble(id = ids, time = 0, amt = drinks$kcal[i], evid = 1L, cmt = "stomach", dvid = NA_integer_)
    obs <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = ids, time = obs_times) |>
      mutate(amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = NA_character_, dvid = 1L)
    bind_rows(dose, obs) |>
      arrange(id, time, desc(evid)) |>
      mutate(drink = drinks$drink[i]) |>
      bind_cols(drinks[i, c("DOSE_FAT_G", "DOSE_CARB_G", "DOSE_PROT_G", "DRINK_OGTT", "FED_HIGHFAT")]) |>
      bind_cols(tibble::as_tibble(subject))
  }))
}
```

# Typical-value checks

## Fasting steady state and closed-form baseline

Before the drink, the initial conditions are the fasting steady state
written in the authors' code. A fasted subject must therefore stay flat.
The baseline plasma TBA concentration then has a closed form,
`base_gb * krb * gb_cc * (1 - EH) / (QH * EH)`.

```{r steady-state}
mod_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(ui)
fasted <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = 1:2, time = seq(0, 600, by = 60)) |>
  mutate(evid = 0L, amt = 0, dvid = 1L, WT = 70, HT = 170, AGE = 64, SEXF = 0, DIS_DIAB = 0,
         DOSE_FAT_G = 10, DOSE_CARB_G = 93, DOSE_PROT_G = 11, DRINK_OGTT = 0,
         FED_HIGHFAT = c(0, 1)[id])
ss <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, fasted, returnType = "data.frame"))

eh_closed <- function(shift) 1 / (1 + exp(-(log(0.638 / 0.362) + shift)))
krb_typ <- log(2) / 1250
cc_closed <- 29.4 * krb_typ * 113 * (1 - eh_closed(c(0, -0.294))) / (1.5 * eh_closed(c(0, -0.294)))

ss_summary <- ss |>
  group_by(id) |>
  summarise(Cc_start = first(Cc), Cc_end = last(Cc), GVol_start = first(GVol), GVol_end = last(GVol)) |>
  mutate(Cc_closed_form = cc_closed[id])
knitr::kable(ss_summary, digits = 4)

stopifnot(
  all(abs(ss_summary$Cc_end / ss_summary$Cc_start - 1) < 1e-6),
  all(abs(ss_summary$GVol_end / ss_summary$GVol_start - 1) < 1e-6),
  all(abs(ss_summary$Cc_start / ss_summary$Cc_closed_form - 1) < 1e-6)
)
```

The typical fasting TBA concentration is 0.70 umol/L for the reference
drinks and 0.93 umol/L on the high-fat occasion. On that occasion the
lower hepatic extraction lets more TBA escape the liver, as Figure 5 of
the paper shows.

## Mass balance of the bile-acid pool

The TBA pool has no source and no sink, so the amount summed over the
gallbladder (volume times 113 mM), the intestine, the liver and the
plasma compartments is constant after a drink.

```{r mass-balance}
ev_typ <- make_events(1)
sim_typ <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, ev_typ, keep = "drink", returnType = "data.frame",
                                         atol = 1e-10, rtol = 1e-10))
pool <- sim_typ |>
  mutate(pool = gallbladder * 113 + bile_upper_si + lower_si1 + lower_si2 + lower_si3 +
           liver + central + peripheral1) |>
  group_by(drink) |>
  summarise(pool_min = min(pool), pool_max = max(pool), rel_range = (max(pool) - min(pool)) / mean(pool))
knitr::kable(pool, digits = 6)
stopifnot(nrow(pool) == 4, all(pool$rel_range < 1e-6))
```

## Typical profiles

```{r typical-profiles, fig.height = 5}
sim_typ |>
  select(drink, time, `Gallbladder volume (mL)` = GVol, `Plasma TBA (umol/L)` = Cc) |>
  pivot_longer(-c(drink, time)) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, value, colour = drink)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~name, scales = "free_y", ncol = 1) +
  labs(x = "Time after test drink (min)", y = NULL, colour = NULL,
       title = "Typical individual: male, 64 y, 70 kg, 1.70 m, no diabetes") +
  theme_bw()
```

# Replication of Figure 5

Figure 5 of the paper shows the median and prediction intervals of
1,000 simulations for a typical individual (no diabetes, male, 70 kg,
1.7 m, 64 years) after each drink. The simulations below use 200 subjects
per drink, with the total (between-subject plus between-occasion)
variability of Table S3. The gastric-emptying variability comes from the
2016 model.

```{r fig5-sim}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20180925)
ev_sto <- make_events(200)
sim_sto <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(ui, ev_sto, keep = "drink", returnType = "data.frame"))

pi_sto <- sim_sto |>
  select(drink, time, GVol, Cc) |>
  pivot_longer(c(GVol, Cc)) |>
  group_by(drink, time, name) |>
  summarise(
    lo95 = quantile(value, 0.025), hi95 = quantile(value, 0.975),
    lo80 = quantile(value, 0.10), hi80 = quantile(value, 0.90),
    median = median(value), .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(name = factor(name, c("GVol", "Cc"), c("Gallbladder volume (mL)", "TBA plasma conc. (umol/L)")))
```

```{r fig5-plot, fig.height = 5.5, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 5 of Guiastrennec 2018: 95% and 80% prediction intervals and median of the simulated gallbladder volume (top) and plasma total bile acids (bottom) after each test drink."}
ggplot(pi_sto, aes(time)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo95, ymax = hi95), fill = "#9ecae1") +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo80, ymax = hi80), fill = "#4292c6") +
  geom_line(aes(y = median)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0) +
  facet_grid(name ~ drink, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Time (min)", y = NULL) +
  theme_bw()
```

The medians at landmark times are compared below with values read by the
maintainers from Figure 5 of the paper (about +/- 0.3 mL and +/- 0.1
umol/L reading precision). Nadir and peak are taken over the simulated
time grid.

```{r fig5-compare}
fig5 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~drink, ~metric, ~published,
  "OGTT 75 g", "GB nadir (mL)", 24.5,
  "Low fat", "GB nadir (mL)", 18.3,
  "Medium fat", "GB nadir (mL)", 16.5,
  "High fat", "GB nadir (mL)", 10.5,
  "OGTT 75 g", "GB at 240 min (mL)", 29.8,
  "Low fat", "GB at 240 min (mL)", 24.6,
  "Medium fat", "GB at 240 min (mL)", 24.4,
  "High fat", "GB at 240 min (mL)", 24.7,
  "OGTT 75 g", "TBA peak (umol/L)", 1.8,
  "Low fat", "TBA peak (umol/L)", 2.1,
  "Medium fat", "TBA peak (umol/L)", 2.45,
  "High fat", "TBA peak (umol/L)", 5.4,
  "OGTT 75 g", "TBA at 240 min (umol/L)", 0.5,
  "Low fat", "TBA at 240 min (umol/L)", 1.6,
  "Medium fat", "TBA at 240 min (umol/L)", 1.8,
  "High fat", "TBA at 240 min (umol/L)", 2.5,
  "OGTT 75 g", "TBA baseline (umol/L)", 0.7,
  "High fat", "TBA baseline (umol/L)", 0.9
)

med <- sim_sto |>
  group_by(drink, time) |>
  summarise(GVol = median(GVol), Cc = median(Cc), .groups = "drop") |>
  group_by(drink) |>
  summarise(
    `GB nadir (mL)` = min(GVol),
    `GB at 240 min (mL)` = GVol[time == 240],
    `TBA peak (umol/L)` = max(Cc),
    `TBA at 240 min (umol/L)` = Cc[time == 240],
    `TBA baseline (umol/L)` = Cc[time == 0]
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(-drink, names_to = "metric", values_to = "simulated") |>
  mutate(drink = as.character(drink))

cmp <- fig5 |>
  left_join(med, by = c("drink", "metric")) |>
  mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (simulated - published) / published)
stopifnot(nrow(cmp) == 18, !anyNA(cmp$simulated))
knitr::kable(cmp, digits = c(0, 0, 2, 2, 1))

# Over 15 cohort draws (seeds 1-14 and the one above, 1 to 16 threads) the
# median difference ranged 0.8 to 7.4% and the 90th percentile of the
# absolute difference 6 to 17%. A mis-transcribed potency, extraction or
# transit time moves these landmarks by tens of percent; reading EH as the
# text's 45.0% raises the high-fat baseline TBA by 60%.
stopifnot(
  abs(median(cmp$pct_diff)) < 12,
  quantile(abs(cmp$pct_diff), 0.9) < 25
)
```

The differences in the table combine the sampling noise of a
200-subject cohort with the reading precision of the figure; none of the
landmarks is systematically off.

The high-fat baseline is the clearest check on how the high-fat effect on
hepatic extraction enters the model. In the authors' code it is added on
the logit scale (EH falls from 63.8% to 56.8%), and this gives a fasting
TBA of 0.93 umol/L, as the figure shows. The text instead describes the
effect as a relative change to 45.0%, which would give
`r signif(29.4 * krb_typ * 113 * 0.55 / (1.5 * 0.45), 3)` umol/L.

# Covariate effects

Type 2 diabetes shortens the basal gallbladder-emptying half-life by
48% and lowers the fat-equivalent sensitivity of gallbladder emptying by
33%. The faster basal emptying raises the fasting TBA concentration, as
the observed means in Figure 1 of the paper show (about 1.8 umol/L in
patients against 1.2 umol/L in controls).

```{r t2d, fig.height = 5}
ev_t2d <- bind_rows(
  make_events(1) |> mutate(group = "Healthy"),
  make_events(1) |> mutate(id = id + 100L, DIS_DIAB = 1, group = "Type 2 diabetes")
)
sim_t2d <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, ev_t2d, keep = c("drink", "group"), returnType = "data.frame"))
sim_t2d |>
  select(drink, group, time, `Gallbladder volume (mL)` = GVol, `Plasma TBA (umol/L)` = Cc) |>
  pivot_longer(-c(drink, group, time)) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, value, colour = drink, linetype = group)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~name, scales = "free_y", ncol = 1) +
  labs(x = "Time after test drink (min)", y = NULL, colour = NULL, linetype = NULL) +
  theme_bw()

base_t2d <- sim_t2d |> filter(time == 0, drink == "Low fat") |> arrange(group)
# Closed form: the fasting concentration scales with krb = log(2) / HLRB.
stopifnot(abs(base_t2d$Cc[2] / base_t2d$Cc[1] - 1 / (1 - 0.481)) < 1e-6)
```

# NCA of the postprandial TBA response

TBA is endogenous, so the NCA below uses the typical postprandial profile
over the 240-minute sampling window. It summarises the size and timing of
the spillover peak for each drink.

```{r nca}
conc <- sim_typ |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  select(id, time, Cc, drink)
dose_df <- ev_typ |>
  filter(evid == 1) |>
  select(id, time, amt, drink)
o_conc <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc, Cc ~ time | drink + id)
o_dose <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | drink + id)
o_data <- PKNCA::PKNCAdata(o_conc, o_dose,
  intervals = data.frame(start = 0, end = 240, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE)
)
nca <- PKNCA::pk.nca(o_data)
nca_tab <- as.data.frame(nca$result) |>
  select(drink, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES) |>
  rename("Cmax (umol/L)" = cmax, "Tmax (min)" = tmax, "AUC0-240 (umol*min/L)" = auclast)
knitr::kable(nca_tab, digits = 1)

cm <- setNames(nca_tab[["Cmax (umol/L)"]], as.character(nca_tab$drink))
au <- setNames(nca_tab[["AUC0-240 (umol*min/L)"]], as.character(nca_tab$drink))
tm <- setNames(nca_tab[["Tmax (min)"]], as.character(nca_tab$drink))
stopifnot(
  length(cm) == 4,
  cm[["High fat"]] > cm[["Medium fat"]], cm[["Medium fat"]] > cm[["Low fat"]],
  au[["High fat"]] > au[["Medium fat"]], au[["Medium fat"]] > au[["Low fat"]],
  tm[["OGTT 75 g"]] < min(tm[c("Low fat", "Medium fat", "High fat")])
)
```

The paper does not report NCA values for TBA. The ordering (high fat >
medium fat > low fat for both Cmax and AUC, with the OGTT peaking earliest)
matches the observed means in Figure 1.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Gastric-emptying parameters.** In the original fit each subject's
  gastric-emptying parameters (KG0, SLPCAL, KUL, T50, SIG) were that
  subject's empirical Bayes estimates from the 2016 model, entered as
  data together with their standard errors. A library model has to
  simulate new subjects, so it uses the 2016 typical values, the 2016
  between-subject variability (CV% = sqrt(omega), the convention of that
  paper's supplementary code) and the 2016 female effect on SLPCAL, all
  fixed. The onset is the logistic function of the 2016 paper's Eq. 3.
  T50 is 15.7 min for the OGTT drink and 23.1 min for any drink with
  `DRINK_OGTT = 0`. All such drinks in this study contain fat. Water was
  not studied.
* **Typographical errors in the published code.** Supplementary Figure S2
  computes `MTCOV = WOM*(1+THETA(17))*...` and then uses an undefined
  `MTTALCOV`. As printed, this would give a zero mean transit time in
  men. It also defines `TVTDUR = TON + THETA(14)` but then uses an
  undefined `TVOFF`. The model follows Eq. 6,
  `(1 - 0.279 * FEM) * (1 + 0.00614 * (CARB - 93))`, and takes the
  refilling offset as `TON + Trefill_duration`, as in Eq. 2.
* **Variability on the refilling offset.** The code puts the eta on the
  offset time `TOFF` (the omega block is labelled `TOFF`), whereas Table 2
  lists that variability under `Trefill_duration`. The model follows the
  code: `trefill_off = (trefill_onset + 156) * exp(eta)`.
* **Logit-scale drink effects.** The code adds the OGTT effect on FAU and
  the high-fat effect on EH on the logit scale. The text reads them as
  relative changes (FAU 48.6% for the OGTT, EH 45.0% for the high-fat
  drink); on the logit scale they give 49.1% and 56.8%. The model follows
  the code. The high-fat fasting baseline in Figure 5 (about 0.9 umol/L)
  agrees with the logit form, and the confidence interval of the high-fat
  effect (-109 to +50%) is only meaningful on that scale.
* **Hepatic blood flow after the drink.** The code multiplies the fasting
  1.5 L/min by 1.3 from the drink onward. The Methods text says 35%,
  while Table 2 prints 2.0 L/min fed, which is consistent with either.
  The model follows the code.
* **Gallbladder additive error.** Table 2 prints 4.27 mL. That is the
  NONMEM `$SIGMA` variance: its confidence interval (1.85 to 6.7) is
  symmetric about 4.27, while the proportional errors are tabulated as
  square roots with asymmetric intervals. The model uses
  SD = sqrt(4.27) = 2.07 mL.
* **Final versus initial estimates.** The `$THETA` and `$OMEGA` values in
  the published code differ from Table 2 and Table S3 in the third
  significant figure (for example HLDJ 2.533 vs 2.52 min). The model uses
  Table 2 for fixed effects and Table S3 for the variance-covariance
  matrix. Fixed physiological constants (VC 2.839 L, VP 4.072 L,
  QD 0.1732 L/min, RAMAX 0.573 x 4 kcal/min, KM 6.28 x 4 kcal) carry the
  code's precision.
* **Total variability.** The paper estimates one eta per parameter for
  between-subject and between-occasion variability together, and gives
  their split only for reference (Table S2). The simulations here draw the
  total variability independently for each subject-occasion; a user who
  needs within-subject correlation across occasions can split each
  variance with Table S2.
* **Energy of the drink.** The NONMEM data carried the energy as a column
  (`KCAL`). Here it is derived from the composition covariates as
  `4 * carbohydrate + 4 * protein + 9 * fat` (Table 1 footnote). The
  `amt` of the stomach dose must equal that value.
* **Before the drink.** The code computes the onset and refilling
  functions on pre-drink records from study time. The model holds the
  fasting steady state until the first dose (no gastric emptying, no
  refilling window, fasting hepatic blood flow), which is the steady
  state its initial conditions assume.
* **Several drinks in one subject.** Each drink above is simulated as a
  separate subject. The authors' data reset the system at each drink
  (NONMEM `EVID = 4`); to simulate a crossover within one subject, dose
  each drink with `evid = 4` so that every occasion starts from the
  fasting steady state.
* **Height units.** The code reads height in metres and multiplies it by
  100 in the DuBois formula. The `HT` covariate here is in centimetres.
